sponsor.evidence: The innovation partner attended the last quarterly review and set the Corporate training date.
The managing partner's office declined two review meetings in June and named no delegate.

demand.evidence: The finance partner stated in June that no further seats will be discussed before renewal.

scenario.label: Synthetic scenario B: high activity, expansion inappropriate
scenario.summary: A well-used account asks for 40 more seats. Activity is high and rising, but fewer than a third of started drafting runs reach an accepted draft, time to an accepted draft has risen, and the lead specialist has no spare hours.

sponsor.evidence: The sponsoring partner joined the firm's management board in June. The successor has not confirmed the programme goals.

demand.evidence: The Innovation Lead asked on 22 July for 40 further seats so that every Corporate associate can use the drafting agent.

expansionCase.proposedScope: 40 further seats for the share purchase agreement first-draft agent across Corporate.

objectives.statement: At least 60% of started drafting runs reach a partner-accepted draft.
Median time to a partner-accepted draft stays below 180 minutes, review and correction included.
Quality failures on no more than 15% of sampled drafts.

scenario.label: Synthetic scenario A: stalled adoption, diagnosed and recovered
scenario.summary: An in-house team activates after training, then stops using the workflow. Diagnosis shows the output did not fit the team's review checklist. After a checklist-mapped playbook and two clinics, repeat use and time to a signed-off result improve over three complete reporting periods.

sponsor.evidence: The General Counsel chaired both follow-up reviews and named an internal owner for the review checklist.

demand.evidence: The General Counsel asked on 20 July to extend the reviewed playbook to Employment and to price six further seats for procurement counsel.

expansionCase.proposedScope: Extend the supplier-contract review playbook to Employment and add six seats for procurement counsel, after a one-period pilot with three Employment lawyers.

objectives.statement: At least 6 of the 8 eligible Corporate lawyers use the supplier-contract review in two or more weeks of each reporting period.
Median time to a signed-off issues list stays below 100 minutes, review and correction included.
Quality failures on no more than 10% of sampled results.
